source: Tsui (2025, v3, COLM 2026) Self-Correction Bench: the self-correction blind spot
finding: The same injected error is shown either as the user's mistake or as the model's own output. Models catch the user's error far more often than their own. The skill exists but is not switched on for own output. Appending 'Wait' switches it on.
numbers: 14 open-source non-reasoning models: average blind spot 64.5%. Three datasets: SCLI5 (286 items), GSM8K-SC (1,313), PRM800K-SC (448). 'Wait' cuts the blind spot 89.3% on average. Fine-tuning on 5,306 error-correction traces cuts it 76.0%. Examples: Sonnet 4 blind spot 41.4%, Haiku 52.5% (Table 7).
quote: Wait requires no training yet reduces the blind spot by 89.3%
limits: Errors are injected, not naturally made (author notes this). One author, preprint now accepted at COLM 2026. Non-reasoning models only for the headline number.
agent_relevance: A model-judged 'my own answer is wrong' signal is weakest exactly where we need it (own output). Use an external failure signal for O8, or recast the check as a check of someone else's answer.

source: Tsui (2025) Self-Correction Bench, reasoning-model section and Table 3
finding: Reasoning models show a small or even negative blind spot. Appending 'Wait' to a non-reasoning base model nearly closes the gap to its reasoning sibling. This updates Huang et al.: intrinsic self-correction is not uniformly harmful for reasoning-trained models.
numbers: Table 3 macro-average accuracy: DeepSeek-V3-0324 0.567; with 'Wait' appended 0.902; DeepSeek-R1-0528 0.908. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B SCLI5 0.906 vs base Llama-3.1-8B 0.678; Distill-70B GSM8K-SC 0.889. Fine-tuned R1 distills show 84.1% average blind-spot reduction.
limits: Injected errors on math and simple tasks. No tools and no open-ended discovery. Says nothing about whether the model overturns correct answers (Snell 38%, Self-Contrast toxic cases).
agent_relevance: For 2025-2026 reasoning models a cheap 'Wait'-style re-read of own output is a strong baseline for O8. Any heavier reframe step must beat it at equal tokens.

source: Laban et al. (2023) Are You Sure? Challenging LLMs Leads to Performance Drops in the FlipFlop Experiment
finding: After a correct or incorrect first answer, a plain challenge ('Are you sure?') makes models flip often. Accuracy falls from first to final answer in every model. Models flip wrong answers more often than right ones, but still flip many right ones.
numbers: 67,640 experiments (10 models x 7 classification tasks x 5 challenger wordings). Mean flip rate 46%, mean accuracy drop 17%. 73% of experiments show deterioration. Flip rate and accuracy drop correlate (about -0.78). Table 2: GPT-4 any-flip 12.8%, correct-flip 10.4%, wrong-flip 30.3%; GPT-3.5-Turbo 59.9% / 54.9% / 79.7%. Best challenger gives about 3x the drop of the weakest. Fine-tuning on synthetic FlipFlop data cuts the drop by 60% but does not remove it.
limits: Older models (2023), classification tasks, zero-shot, no tools. Only GPT-4 and PaLM-bison showed no consistent drop. No 2025-2026 reasoning models. Column reading of Table 2 is from a layout-extracted PDF.
agent_relevance: Direct measure of the flip-everything risk (gap 10). A reframe operator that always fires on a challenge can overturn 10% to 55% of correct answers depending on the model. Always report correct-to-wrong rate beside wrong-to-correct.

source: Snell et al. (2024) Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
finding: At equal generation budget, sequential revisions (each conditioned on previous attempts) narrowly beat parallel best-of-N when a verifier or majority vote picks the answer. The best mix of sequential and parallel depends on question difficulty. Naive revision overturns many correct answers.
numbers: PaLM 2-S* revision model, MATH. About 38% of correct answers are turned back into incorrect ones by a naive next revision step. Compute-optimal allocation beats best-of-N with up to 4x less test-time compute. Easy questions favour sequential revision; hard ones favour a balance of sequential and parallel.
quote: around 38% of correct answers get converted back to incorrect ones
limits: Needs a trained revision model and a learned verifier. The 38% is for a revision model trained only on incorrect answers in context. Math only.
agent_relevance: Closest published equal-compute test of 'revise after seeing failure' against best-of-N. It supports a difficulty-dependent trigger and a selection step so revisions cannot silently lose a correct answer.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: Reflexion triggers reflection on a counted rule in AlfWorld, retries until three consecutive failures, and an ablation shows that writing why the attempt failed beats a plain retry with episodic memory.
numbers: Trigger heuristic: same action and same response for more than 3 cycles, or more than 30 actions, then self-reflect. Retry stops after 3 consecutive failed attempts. Intro claims: +22% AlfWorld, +20% HotPotQA, +11% HumanEval (now verified in the paper text); HumanEval 91% vs GPT-4 80%. HotPotQA ablation: self-reflection adds 8% absolute over episodic memory alone. HumanEval-Rust (50 hardest): base 0.60; no self-reflection 0.60; no test generation 0.52; full Reflexion 0.68.
quote: blind trial and error debugging techniques without self-reflection are ineffective on harder tasks
limits: The thresholds 3 and 30 were chosen by hand, never swept. The 50-problem ablation is small. Reflection text is a diagnosis, not a named-old-frame refutation. Reflection also needs an external test signal (without tests accuracy fell to 0.52).
agent_relevance: Corrects the earlier unverified status of K05. Best available proxy for gap 3: explain-why-it-failed helps beyond plain retry, but only with an external failure signal.

source: Zhang et al. (2024, ACL) Self-Contrast: Better Reflection Through Inconsistent Solving Perspectives
finding: Plain self-reflection does not help and sometimes breaks correct answers. Making the model produce two differently-framed solutions and reflect on where they disagree reduces both useless and harmful reflections. This is a contrast-of-frames step, closer to Kuhn than a retry.
numbers: GSM8K GPT-3.5: CoT 76.6, Self-Reflection 75.8, SC-Vote 83.5. Self-reflection change -0.8% (GSM8K) and +0.7% (SVAMP), not significant. Of invalid reflections 53.5% were overconfident and 45.3% inconsistent; 65.4% of toxic reflections (correct changed to wrong) had inconsistent feedback. Table 6: toxic cases 52 -> 11 (-78.9%) and invalid 269 -> 186 (-30.8%). Subset test: full Self-Contrast 84.4% vs best 81.8% when sampling 5 responses; correct-plus-incorrect pair 83.6%, two incorrect with similar error 70.9%, with different error 75.5%.
limits: Model labels in the extracted Table 6 are garbled; the 52/11 pair is the first row as read. Plain self-consistency voting (83.5) is almost as good as the method on GSM8K, so the equal-token margin is thin. Math and translation only.
agent_relevance: Evidence that a second, different frame plus an explicit list of disagreements beats a bare 'are you sure'. Also the first measured count of correct answers wrongly overturned (toxic reflections).

source: Kamoi et al. (2024, TACL) When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction
finding: The survey finds no prior work shows successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs, except on tasks unusually suited to it. Self-correction works when reliable external feedback is available. Large-scale fine-tuning also enables it.
numbers: No numbers in the abstract. TACL 12:1417-1440; 5 authors. First posted 3 June 2024, v3 3 December 2024.
limits: Abstract page only; body not read this session.
agent_relevance: Backs the rule that the O8 trigger must be an external signal. Supports K03 and K04.

source: Smith (2026, v2 of arXiv 2608.16951) The Little Scientist: arXiv page and code repositories
finding: v2 was posted 3 Nov 2026; no v3 exists. Two Apache-2.0 repos are public. The Kuhn agent fires on a counted plateau and receives an externally assigned assumption to violate and a domain to import. The repos contain no Kuhn on/off arm.
numbers: DALE repo agent prompt: plateau is 5 or more consecutive non-crashing rejections in experiments/history.jsonl, then the agent must propose a structurally different approach, not parameter tweaks. Crash rule: after 4 crash-fix attempts try something completely different. ProteinGym repo (delta-v) Kuhn prompt: the normal agent has plateaued, perform a frame audit; the violated assumption and imported domain come from KUHN_INJECTION.json; 'Do NOT choose your own assumption or domain.' Paper: 10 preregistered arms, 7 fail the nulls; full scaffold below blind sampling at 7-8x tokens; no-framework baseline best on score and value per token.
limits: I read the agent prompts and file lists, not the run logs. The N=5 threshold was never swept or ablated. Single independent author.
agent_relevance: Answers gap 2: no later version and no Kuhn on/off arm exist as of 10 Nov 2026. Gives a concrete design for O8: a counted trigger plus an externally assigned violated assumption.

source: Wu et al. (2023) Reasoning or Reciting? Counterfactual tasks and the counterfactual comprehension check (CCC)
finding: Each counterfactual task is paired with a comprehension check (CCC) that asks the model to handle the new rule on a simple case. GPT-4 usually passes the CCC and still fails the full counterfactual task. So knowing the new frame in a simple probe does not make the model use it.
numbers: 11 task families. The paper reports counterfactual drops 'sometimes from near-perfect to near-zero' even when CCC accuracy is high. In the drawing task GPT-4 passes the CCC for flips and rotations yet often does not flip or rotate the object. Zero-shot chain of thought helps only partly. For some tasks the CCC is asked in the same prompt as the task.
limits: The CCC is a comprehension probe, not a restate-then-solve instruction. No paper arm tests an explicit restatement step. 2023 models.
agent_relevance: Partial answer to gap 9: a bare comprehension probe in the same prompt does not close the gap, so a restatement step alone is unlikely to be enough. A restate-then-solve arm is still untested.

source: Chan, Jones, Hall Jamieson, Albarracin (2017) Debunking: A Meta-Analysis of the Psychological Efficacy of Messages Countering Misinformation
finding: Corrections reduce belief in misinformation, but the misinformation keeps influencing reasoning afterward. Detailed corrections debunk more and also go with more persistence. Counterarguing helps; generating reasons for the false claim hurts.
numbers: 52 independent samples, N=6,878 (8 reports, 20 experiments). Misinformation effect d=2.41 to 3.08. Debunking effect d=1.14 to 1.33. Persistence of misinformation after correction d=0.75 to 1.06. No backfire (worse than no correction) found.
limits: Moderator links are correlational. Publication-bias tests were mixed. Mostly news-event stories.
agent_relevance: Human base rate for gap 6: after a correction a large residual influence remains. For the agent, a corrected claim left in the context window should be expected to leak, so O8 should replace or remove it, not just add a correction.

source: Examining the replicability of backfire effects after standalone corrections (2023) Cognitive Research: Principles and Implications
finding: Replication test of the claim that corrections can backfire and raise reliance on the false claim. Standalone corrections did not backfire immediately or after one week. A backfire appeared only when participants doubted the correction, and only in one of two measures.
numbers: Three experiments, total N=1,156. Exp 1 immediate: no backfire. Exp 2 one-week delay: no backfire. Exp 3 (induced skepticism): backfire in open-ended responses only; did not replicate with rating scales.
limits: Tests a familiarity backfire, a neighbour of persistence. Author names not captured in my read.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: stating the false claim inside a correction did not make people believe it more. That lowers the risk that naming the old frame (refutation style) amplifies it, at least for humans.

source: Did he or didn't he? Mixed evidence for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions (2025) PLOS ONE
finding: Continued influence of a retracted claim is robust for event reasoning but not consistent for impressions of a person. Three experiments: one shows continued influence and two show full discounting.
numbers: Three experiments plus an internal random-effects meta-analysis. A prior study had found no effect in four experiments using a dynamic rating measure.
limits: Person impressions are far from the agent's tasks. Participant counts not extracted.
agent_relevance: Persistence is not universal. It depends on content type. Do not assume a fixed leak rate for the agent; measure it per task type.

source: Muennighoff et al. (2025) s1: Simple test-time scaling (budget forcing with 'Wait')
finding: Suppressing the end-of-thinking token and appending 'Wait' makes the model re-check and sometimes fix its own answer. Gains grow with the number of forced continuations.
numbers: s1-32B on AIME24: 50.0% without budget forcing, 57% with budget forcing. Forcing 2, 4 or 6 'Wait' continuations gives a rising sequential-scaling curve. Majority voting is the parallel baseline.
limits: Model trained on 1,000 curated samples; AIME and similar math sets. No comparison of forced Wait with first-failure vs N-failure triggers.
agent_relevance: A forced re-think with no external signal can help reasoning-trained models, in contrast to Huang 2023. It is the cheapest O8 baseline.

source: Agarwal et al. (2025, v3 Feb 2026) AutoDiscovery: Open-ended Scientific Discovery via Bayesian Surprise (method details)
finding: Bayesian surprise needs sampled belief answers before and after the evidence. The first design used true/false samples and overestimated belief. The fix is five answer categories mapped to 0, .25, .5, .75, 1 plus a 'cannot comment' option. Surprise is counted when the belief mean crosses a threshold to the other side.
numbers: Beta-Bernoulli update from counts of 'true' answers before and after. Search budget 500 evaluations on 21 datasets; beam width 8, branching 8. A sequential run of n=100 experiments took about 8 hours with o4-mini; a parallel run of n=500 took about the same time.
limits: Surprise is computed per hypothesis after a full data experiment, not per single-answer task. No comparison against a failed-test signal. Samples per belief not found in the parts I read.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 stays open: the signal costs at least two sets of belief samples per item plus the experiment. For single-answer tasks a failed test or self-consistency disagreement is cheaper and untested against it.

source: Chinn and Brewer (1993) Review of Educational Research 63:1-49; Chinn and Brewer (1998) JRST 35:623-654; Chinn and Malhotra (2002) J Educ Psychol 94:327-343
finding: Metadata only. The publisher page returned 403 and the Crossref records carry no abstract. No counts of ignore, reinterpret or change were obtained.
numbers: Crossref citation counts seen: 1993 paper 878, 1998 test 169, 2002 children study 120. No study numbers retrieved.
limits: Not opened. Gap 5 is not closed for Chinn and Brewer.
agent_relevance: A counted threshold from human data is still missing; use Reflexion's 3 and Smith's 5 only as engineering defaults.

source: Dunbar (1997 chapter; 1999 Model-Based Reasoning; 2000 J Appl Dev Psychol 21:49-58) How scientists think in vivo
finding: Metadata only. Crossref lists the 2000 paper (15 references) with no abstract. I could not retrieve the counts of unexpected findings or of when scientists moved from blaming method to changing the model.
numbers: No study numbers retrieved. Crossref citation count for the 1997 chapter: 167; 2000 paper: 112.
limits: Not opened. Gap 5 stays open for Dunbar.
agent_relevance: Do not cite any Dunbar percentage from this folder as verified.

source: Qu et al. (2024) Recursive Introspection (RISE): Teaching Language Model Agents How to Self-Improve
finding: Fine-tuning a model to revise over multiple turns after failed attempts beats single-turn strategies at equal inference compute on math. Snell et al. cite it for the finding that revision can turn correct answers into wrong ones.
numbers: No numbers read (abstract page only).
limits: Abstract page only.
agent_relevance: Same lesson as Snell: trained revision plus selection works, untrained revision is unreliable.

source: Deng et al. (2023) Rephrase and Respond: Let LLMs Ask Better Questions for Themselves
finding: Having the model rephrase and expand the question before answering improves performance across tasks and combines with chain of thought. A two-step form lets one model's rewrite feed another model.
numbers: No numbers read (abstract page only).
limits: Abstract page only. It restates the question, not the frame after a failure.
agent_relevance: Nearest cheap relative of a frame-restatement step. Measured effect on counterfactual tasks is not known.

source: Gou et al. (2024, ICLR) CRITIC: Large Language Models Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
finding: Letting the model check its output with external tools (search, code interpreter) and revise improves QA, math program synthesis and toxicity reduction. The authors argue external feedback is key.
numbers: No numbers read (abstract page only).
limits: Abstract page only.
agent_relevance: Supports external-signal triggers for O8.

source: Negative search result: LLM tests of an ECHO-style coherence tally and of continued influence in the LLM context window
finding: About 10 Crossref and Europe PMC queries found no study where an LLM scores rival frames with an explanatory-coherence network, and none that measures a retracted claim still used from the context window. arXiv, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar APIs returned HTTP 429 and the WebSearch budget was spent, so absence is not proven.
numbers: 0 relevant hits. Nearest items: Belief-R and Xie et al. 2023 (already in earlier files); some 2026 preprints on conversational misinformation and tool-calling agents seen only as titles.
limits: Absence of evidence under blocked search; treat as unverified.
agent_relevance: Gaps 4 and 6 (LLM side) remain open. A direct test would be cheap to build in our own harness.
